topics.title: Microservices
topics.description: Decomposition, resilience and data ownership questions that open most architecture rounds.

key_areas.description: Decomposing a monolith requires identifying bounded contexts and establishing clear service boundaries.
Circuit breakers, bulkheads, timeouts and retries so that one failing service does not take the system down.
Each service owns its data. Introduce CQRS and event sourcing where the read and write models genuinely diverge.

communication: Asynchronous: Kafka, RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, AWS SQS and SNS

topics.title: REST API Design
topics.description: Maturity levels, status codes, versioning and API security.
richardson_maturity_model: Level 0: a single endpoint, usually POST only
Level 2: HTTP verbs used correctly (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)

design_rules.description: Use the appropriate HTTP status code: 2xx success, 4xx client errors, 5xx server errors.
Version the API through the URL, a header, or content negotiation.
Use OAuth 2.0 and JWT for authentication and authorization.

topics.title: Event-Driven Architecture
topics.description: Event styles and the trade-offs an interviewer expects you to name unprompted.

patterns.description: Simple notifications that a state change happened; consumers call back for details.
Events carry the data payload so consumers do not need to call back.
Events are the system of record; current state is a fold over the event log.
Separate read and write models, each optimized for its own access pattern.

topics.title: Design Patterns
topics.description: The classic catalogue plus where each one actually shows up in a Spring codebase.

topics.title: Distributed Systems
topics.description: CAP, consensus and the three ways to keep a transaction consistent across services.

fundamentals.description: Under a network partition you choose between consistency and availability; the trade-off drives the datastore choice.
Raft and Paxos: how a cluster agrees on a single value or leader.
Eureka and Consul let services find each other without hardcoded addresses.

topics.title: Java Memory & Concurrency
topics.description: JVM memory areas, garbage collection, and the concurrency toolkit from threads up to virtual threads.

memory_model.description: Object storage; the area tuned and collected by the garbage collector.
Method calls and local variables, one stack per thread.
Class metadata, native memory, replaced PermGen in Java 8.

garbage_collection: Memory leaks: common causes such as unbounded caches, static references and unclosed resources
JVM options for tuning heap size and pause targets

concurrency.description: A thread is a lightweight execution unit inside a process; a process has its own memory space.
New, Runnable, Blocked, Waiting, Timed Waiting, Terminated.
ThreadLocal for thread-scoped variables; pools of type Fixed, Cached, Scheduled and ForkJoinPool.
The synchronized keyword, ReentrantLock, atomic classes, and volatile for visibility.
ExecutorService, CompletableFuture, reactive programming with Project Reactor, and virtual threads in Java 21.

topics.title: Java Language Core
topics.description: Functional programming, collections and exception handling as they come up in scenario questions.

functional_programming.description: Transformations map, flatMap and filter; terminal operations collect, reduce and forEach.
Handling absent values safely instead of returning null.

exception_handling.description: Checked exceptions must be declared or handled (IOException); unchecked are runtime exceptions (NullPointerException).
Create one when callers need to react differently; otherwise reuse the standard hierarchy.
Automatic resource management for anything implementing AutoCloseable.
Fail fast, never swallow exceptions, log with context, and clean up resources deterministically.

topics.title: Spring Framework
topics.description: Core container, web layer, data access, security and the Spring Cloud stack.

spring_core.description: BeanFactory vs ApplicationContext, bean lifecycle, and scopes: singleton, prototype, request, session, application.
Constructor injection is preferred; setter and field injection exist but hide dependencies.
Auto-configuration, starters, Actuator, and externalized configuration.

spring_web.description: @Controller vs @RestController, @RequestMapping and its variants, and request-binding annotations.
ResponseEntity for explicit status and headers; centralized error handling with @ControllerAdvice.
Supported media types selected through the Accept header.

spring_data.description: Derived query methods, the @Query annotation, plus paging and sorting.
@Transactional with its propagation types and isolation levels.

spring_security.description: In-memory, JDBC and LDAP providers; OAuth2 and JWT; a custom UserDetailsService.
Role-based access control, method security with @PreAuthorize and @PostAuthorize, and security expressions.
Protection mechanisms and their configuration for browser and API clients.

topics.title: Databases & Caching
topics.description: SQL, NoSQL, ORM performance and the cache patterns behind them.

sql.description: ACID properties, isolation levels, and locking mechanisms.
Indexing strategies, query rewriting, and reading execution plans.

nosql: Each type sits at a different point of the CAP trade-off; choose by access pattern, not by hype

orm_and_jpa.description: One-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many, with eager versus lazy loading.
JPA is the specification; Hibernate is the most common implementation.
Solve the N+1 problem with fetch joins or entity graphs, use batch processing, and apply first and second level caching.

caching.description: In-memory such as Ehcache and Caffeine; distributed such as Redis and Hazelcast.
TTL expiry and explicit invalidation strategies.

topics.title: Observability
topics.description: Metrics, logging, tracing and health checks: what to instrument and with which tool.
metrics: Types: business, application, system and custom metrics
Tools: Micrometer, Prometheus, Grafana, New Relic
logging: Structured logging in JSON so logs can be parsed by machines
Centralized logging with the ELK stack or Graylog
tracing: Distributed tracing with Zipkin, Jaeger or OpenTelemetry
Trace context propagated as TraceID and SpanID
Visualized as trace graphs and service maps
health_checks: Liveness probes: is the process alive
Readiness probes: can it accept traffic
Startup probes: has slow initialization finished
Implemented through Spring Boot Actuator health endpoints

topics.title: DevOps & CI/CD
topics.description: Containers, pipelines, testing strategy and infrastructure as code.

containerization.description: Dockerfile best practices, multi-stage builds, and Docker Compose for local stacks.
Pods, Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, StatefulSets, and Helm charts for packaging.

pipelines: Stages: build, test (unit, integration, end-to-end), deploy, verify
Tools: Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps
Strategies: blue-green deployment, canary releases, feature flags

testing_strategy.description: Many unit tests with JUnit and Mockito, fewer integration tests with TestContainers, few end-to-end tests.
REST Assured, Pact for contract testing, Postman and Newman for collections.

topics.title: Security
topics.description: Authentication protocols, the OWASP Top 10, and secure coding habits.

authentication_and_authorization.description: Grant types, token types and the flows appropriate to each client.
Structure of header, payload and signature; validation rules and best practices around expiry and secret rotation.

secure_coding.description: Sanitize input and use parameterized queries everywhere.
HTML and JavaScript encoding at the point of rendering.
HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS; never secrets in source control.

topics.title: Scenario Questions
topics.description: Open-ended how-would-you questions, with the bullet answer to talk through.

architecture.question: How would you scale an e-commerce system?
answer: Identify the bottlenecks: database, API layer, static content
Serve static content from a CDN
Move order processing to an event-driven architecture

architecture.question: How would you break a monolith into microservices?
answer: Apply the strangler pattern rather than a big-bang rewrite
Ensure data consistency across the new services
Add service discovery and an API gateway

architecture.question: Design a distributed logging system.
answer: Collection agents on each host or pod

implementation.question: How would you handle concurrent updates to the same resource?
answer: Optimistic locking with a version column
Pessimistic locking when contention is high
Event sourcing so writes are appends rather than updates

implementation.question: How would you ensure data consistency in a microservices architecture?
answer: Two-phase commit where a coordinator is acceptable

implementation.question: How would you handle distributed transactions?

performance.question: How would you diagnose and fix a slow API endpoint?
answer: Profile the code to find where time is spent
Add caching where the data allows it
Move slow work to asynchronous processing

performance.question: How would you optimize database performance?
answer: Shard when a single node is no longer enough

security_scenarios.question: How would you secure an API?
answer: An API gateway as the single entry point

security_scenarios.question: How would you handle sensitive data?
answer: Data masking in logs and lower environments

devops_scenarios.question: How would you implement CI/CD for a microservices architecture?
answer: Decide the repository structure: monorepo versus multiple repositories
Define the build strategy per service
Define the testing strategy across the pyramid
Choose deployment strategies such as blue-green or canary

devops_scenarios.question: How would you handle database migrations in a CI/CD pipeline?
answer: Version migrations with Liquibase or Flyway
Use blue-green deployments so old and new schema coexist
Version the database alongside the application
